svg.title: Graphical abstract: controlled replication and cross-kinase generalization study of zero-shot protein language model sensitivity to kinase-inhibitor resistance
svg.desc: Pipeline showing a kinase panel of MET (replication gate), EGFR (background-aware scoring) and ABL1 (controlled delta-pIC50 benchmark) with clinically observed resistance mutations, scored by zero-shot ESM-1b/ESM-2 protein language models at multiple sizes with no task-specific fine-tuning, compared against non-learned baselines (BLOSUM62, conservation, distance to inhibitor and ATP pocket), evaluated against experimental reference measurements split into untreated baseline fitness and drug-treated resistance, analyzed with per-kinase per-drug per-model correlations, bootstrap confidence intervals, paired comparisons and multiple-comparison correction, gated on first reproducing the published MET result before generalizing to EGFR and ABL1.
svg.text: Can Protein-Language-Model Scale Improve Zero-Shot Identification of Kinase-Inhibitor Resistance?
Controlled replication and cross-kinase generalization: MET (replication gate) → EGFR (background-aware) → ABL1 (controlled ΔpIC50)
no DMS dataset exists — ChEMBL only
same tiering applied to EGFR + ABL1
ρ per kinase, per drug, per model
pattern hold for EGFR/ABL1, and for
novelty = controlled test of whether scale
Rigor for Q1: preregistered analysis plan · open data + scoring code release · explicit explanation if scale does not improve prediction over baselines
Does protein-language-model scale improve zero-shot identification of drug-specific kinase-inhibitor
resistance beyond what simple evolutionary and structural baselines already capture — or is drug-
specific resistance simply not recoverable from sequence alone?
Builds on Estevam et al. 2025, eLife 13:RP101882 (MET, ESM-1b only; r≈0.28→0.37 max with 13 added features)
